clause_evidence.reasoning: Nine samples employ set_click interaction requiring students to actively shade specified fractional amounts on visual models. These shading tasks directly assess the representation competency across multiple denominators.
Nine samples employ read_mcq format requiring students to identify which fraction label correctly represents a visual model. These identification tasks directly support the competency requirement.

The competency explicitly requires similar fractions, typically meaning equivalent fractions or recognition of the same amount in different representations. While samples include 2/4 appearing twice, there is no comparative task demonstrating that 2/4 equals 1/2 or any equivalent fraction recognition. This concept is entirely absent from assessment.

Analysis of all eighteen samples reveals complete absence of fractions with denominators 2 and 3. Only denominators 4, 5, 6, and 8 appear across the packet. This represents a critical gap in the required denominator range specified by the competency.

All eighteen samples employ either FractionModel or FractionShade visual types, which represent fractions through geometric models and visual partitioning rather than discrete groups of countable objects. Traditional groups of objects representation using items like apples, stars, or other counters is entirely absent.

Nine samples employ FractionModel visual type with partitioned wholes and shaded portions, functioning as fraction charts. These visual models directly support the requirement for fraction chart representation.

Nine samples employ FractionShade visual type with equal rectangular sections that function as fraction tiles. Students either identify or shade portions of these tile arrangements, demonstrating use of the tile representation method.

Two samples explicitly reference number line representation in the stem, with FractionModel visuals displaying endpoints labeled 0 and 1. These samples directly address the number line representation method specified in the competency.
